sources.title: Tertiary mammal beds of Virgin Valley and Thousand Creek in northwestern Nevada, Part II: Vertebrate faunas
sources.location: Original figure page with figs. 78a–b, 79 and 80; inspected scan captions identify No. 11886, type No. 11880 and form-B No. 11892.
sources.supports: Selected species and type-fragment identity; distal lateral and cross-sectional shape; posterior basal ridge above the orbit. Figure 80 is comparative only.
sources.limitations: Separate fragments, not a complete skull, paired horn set or postcranial skeleton. The Commons generic date field says 1902, but the linked volume and cited paper are 1911; do not use the incorrect mirror date as publication date.
sources.rights: Primary scan is marked US public domain on the image record; used for anatomical consultation only.
sources.verification: Downloaded original 1931 × 2576 scan and inspected the actual figure pixels and captions on 2026-10-24.

sources.title: Extending the utility of artiodactyl postcrania for species-level identifications using multivariate morphometric analyses
sources.authors: Edward Byrd Davis and Jonathan Jean-Michel Calède
sources.location: Figure 1.2 on printed p. 2, introduction p. 3, discussion/conclusion pp. 12–14.
sources.supports: Photographed I. alexandrae spiraled horncore; Thousand Creek late Miocene context; limits of associating isolated postcrania and interpreting two named Ilingoceros species.
sources.limitations: The figure is a fragment and does not determine complete tip, sheath or whole-body proportions. Its caption gives no securely transcribed catalog number, so none is invented.
sources.rights: Article states copyright Society of Vertebrate Paleontology, January 2012. Public reference link only; no article text, photographs or diagrams incorporated in model or public files.
sources.verification: Downloaded the 22-page PDF once; read relevant text and inspected rasterized printed p. 2 at 1600-pixel height on 2026-10-24.

sources.title: Pronghorn, Yellowstone National Park
sources.authors: U.S. National Park Service; photograph credited NPS / Neal Herbert
sources.location: Behavior & Size, Description, and lead adult-pronghorn photograph; updated April 17, 2025.
sources.supports: Explicit extant analog for slender quadrupedal body organization, short tail, head/ear placement and illustrative pronghorn-sized scale.
sources.limitations: Antilocapra americana is not Ilingoceros. Its short hooked/pronged horns, exact coat pattern, performance and shedding schedule must not be transferred as fossil facts.
sources.rights: Image credited NPS / Neal Herbert; consulted privately only, not incorporated. No blanket license assumed for all page content.
